home.title: Can you actually get out at the printed price?
home.subtitle: Executable cash-exit capacity for Solana tokenized equities and stock-quoted launches — measured, not estimated.
home.productLine: Liquidity Depth Scanner — executable exit capacity for Solana tokenized equities.
home.whatBody: A hosted probe engine that asks Jupiter for real sell quotes at escalating order sizes, then scores how much USDC you actually receive versus the printed market cap. It detects routing cliffs, no-route walls, and binding legs that TVL dashboards cannot see.

why.title: Why this tool is essential
why.subtitle: Six findings from live measurement — not theory.

sections.title: The printed price is not the exit price
sections.body: STONK shows $215M on-chain market cap. A $1M cash exit recovers only 85%. Printed valuation and executable exit capacity are different numbers — and the gap can be enormous.

sections.title: The metric everyone publishes is the wrong one
sections.body: Pool TVL ÷ market cap correlates at ρ = −0.66 with measured exit cost. Absolute pool TVL reaches ρ = −0.92. Normalising by valuation actively destroys signal. SPYx ranks worst by TVL/mcap ratio (5.3%) yet executes $100k at 9 basis points.

sections.title: Cliffs are invisible to every existing dashboard
sections.body: STRCx executes cleanly at $150k, then returns $0.04 per token at $200k because the router switches paths. TVL, volume, and price are unchanged. Only a size-dependent quote probe reveals this.

sections.title: Hard walls matter more than big slippage numbers
sections.body: 6 of 18 probed assets return no route at $250k. FTR fails above $25k. A no-route ceiling is a harder capacity limit than any slippage percentage.

sections.title: You may not hold the asset you think you do
sections.body: Searching for HOODx returns ~20 tokens. One embeds the genuine mint address inside its own name field to defeat string matching. Mint-level authentication is a prerequisite, not a feature.

sections.title: Quoted depth is not committed depth
sections.body: Much of the good depth on majors comes from RFQ venues (Riptide, Byreal, AlphaQ) that can withdraw precisely under stress. The scanner tags RFQ share separately instead of merging it into one depth number.

methodology.title: How we measure
methodology.subtitle: Open, timestamped, reproducible — not a black-box score.

steps.title: Micro-quote baseline
steps.body: A $200 sell quote establishes the execution price baseline. All ladder rungs measure relative impact against this baseline, not against the external oracle price. This separates size-dependent slippage from premium/discount to reference.

steps.title: Sell ladder
steps.body: Seven notionals: $1k, $10k, $50k, $100k, $250k, $500k, $1M. For each, we request a Jupiter sell quote (token → USDC) and take the median of 3 samples.

steps.title: Cliff bisection
steps.body: When adjacent rungs show >15% efficiency drop AND route composition changes, we bisect between them to refine the cliff boundary.

steps.title: Scoring
steps.body: Exit capacity at 99%/95%/90% thresholds via log-linear interpolation. No-route ceiling, mcap-to-exit ratio, RFQ dependence, cliff detection, and letter grades A–F.

steps.title: Guards against known bugs
steps.body: Decimals always from Jupiter price/v3 API — never assumed. Flat-across-sizes curves with nonzero offset are rejected (external-price baseline error). Regression fixtures lock SPYx, STONK, STRCx cliff, and FTR no-route.

methodology.disclaimer: This tool measures executable router quotes at probe time. It does not predict future liquidity, guarantee execution, or constitute investment advice. Past probe results do not guarantee future exit capacity.
